thread:
sam: quick sync on resume/token surface. were oscillating between tiny opaque handles and richer cursor objects. need a decision
nina: constraints: py ergonomics (hide complexity), ts web ergonomics (explicit tokens common), go perf (avoid allocations)
carlos: enumerate: tiny opaque handle (string) vs structured cursor ({stream,offset,crc}) vs ephemeral local-state in SDK + server handle
eva: transport mapping: streaming (grpc/ws) prefers local state + small server handle; unary/paged requires a stable token in request body
sam: retries: streaming auto-resume on transient errors seems reasonable; for paged/unary avoid auto-resume by default to prevent side-effect duplication
carlos: token format: version field mandatory. prefer server-side opaque but allow dev-mode decode in SDK for debugging. never embed raw user content
nina: python API idea: iterator that yields items and optionally a token when resume_tokens=True; auto_resume=True by default for iterables
eva: ts API: explicit token methods to fit browser patterns: getResumeToken(), resumeFrom(token). default no auto-resume
carlos: go API: small ResumeHandle struct with fixed fields (ver uint8, seq uint64) and ResumeFrom(handle) call. zero-copy where possible
sam: lifecycle: default TTL 4h; enterprise opt-in for longer via header. server emits Deprecation header for old token versions
build-bot: (ci) note: changes require runtime handshake bump and e2e tests. coordinate with eng-runtime and security for token format review
nina: next steps: i'll draft py/ts stubs; carlos will sketch go. followup API review next week; owners assigned
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
